newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher in dull trade Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher in dull trade Monday.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities crept higher in thin trade by late afternoon Monday, with discount coupons rising a modest 5/32.
Trading activity was sidelined as Presidential and Congressional elections loom, traders said.
"We're just waiting for the election results," said one New York-based trader. "If Democrats come up with a big victory (in Congress), maybe we trade off and mortgages don't do so well."

The trader said he purchased a large chunk of Ginnie Mae II 30-year 8.5 percent coupons, "which have some big prepayment risks to be sure but for banks make a lot of sense." He declined to comment on the size of the deal.
No major bid lists were cited Monday, traders said.
By late afternoon, pass-throughs were 2/32 to 6/32 higher. Spreads over Treasuries mostly held firm.

Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 5/32 at 100-13/32 to yield 113 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was up 5/32 as well, at 100-09/32 and 100-13/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was up 6/32 at 101-03/32, yielding 6.35 percent.
On Wednesday, as part of its quarterly refunding, the Treasury will auction a fresh supply of $10.0 billion in 10-year Treasury notes.
